name: interview-tts
preparation:
## RoleOrTopic
Interviewing for a Senior Backend Engineer position on a payments platform team.
## Contribution
At Northwind Payments (2021-2024) I designed and led the idempotency layer for the card-capture API, with one other engineer. I wrote the design doc and the reconciliation job.
## VerifiedResults
Duplicate captures fell from about 40 per week to zero over the following quarter. The reconciliation job runs nightly over roughly 2 million transactions in under 15 minutes.
## Limitations
The idempotency keys were kept for 24 hours only, so very late client retries were not covered.
## Terminology
idempotency key, exactly-once, outbox pattern, Kafka, PostgreSQL

lines.speaker: I
lines.text: Thanks for joining today. Let's start with a technical question.

lines.speaker: I
lines.text: How would you design a payment API so that a client retry never charges the customer twice? And what happens if the database commit succeeds but the response is lost?

lines.speaker: J
lines.text: Let me follow up on that. Why not just rely on exactly-once delivery from Kafka instead of building idempotency keys yourself?

lines.speaker: I
lines.text: Okay. Tell me about a time you made a production system more reliable. What exactly did you do, and what was the measurable result?
